$schema-note: Capabilities 001-chromatic-guitar-tuner put explicitly out of scope. Any surface that describes this product — the web page's identity, either store listing, the privacy policy — must not claim one, including inside a negation (FR-093, FR-110, contract L5).
$why-one-file: This list had one consumer (apps/web/e2e/metadata.spec.ts) and 004 gives it a second and third: the iOS listing and the Android listing. Principle I places extraction at the third occurrence. The hazard is also asymmetric in a way ordinary duplication is not — a term missing from one copy of the list does not fail, it silently permits the claim it was written to forbid.
$why-regex-source-strings: JSON is the only format all three consumers already speak (research D1: CI pins Node 20, so the gate is .mjs and cannot import a .ts module). Storing the pattern source rather than a plain word keeps word-boundary matching, which is the property that makes the list usable at all.
$why-word-boundaries: Matched with \b rather than as substrings. Nothing authored today trips a naive `includes` — that was checked, not assumed — but the hazard is one ordinary word away: `async` contains `sync` and `accounting` contains `account`. A gate that reports a violation for prose containing nothing wrong gets muted, and a muted gate protects nothing. Compile with new RegExp(source, 'i') on every side.
